incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code of Commerce, articles L223-1 and subsequent articles
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital requirement of €1 fully paid-up and deposited in a blocked bank account; no escrow account mandated
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial share capital of the SARL is subscribed by the shareholder(s) in the amount of one Euro (€1.00), fully paid-up and deposited in a blocked bank account. The registered office of the company is adopted at [insert complete French address]. The following persons are appointed as managers: [full name of manager 1] and [full name of manager 2]. All managers are vested with full powers to manage the company's business, sign all acts and contracts, represent the company vis-à-vis third parties, and open any bank accounts. This resolution is adopted effective immediately upon registration of the company with the Commercial Register (RCS) and publication in the Official Journal. The corporate purpose includes the conduct of battery safety testing in compliance with UN38.3 standards and CE-RED electromagnetic compatibility requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French notary and guichet-entreprises.fr online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a French notary to draft the articles of association specifying the company name, registered office, share capital, managers, and corporate purpose. Deposit the minimum capital of €1 in a blocked bank account. Submit the signed articles and supporting documents via the guichet-entreprises.fr online portal for preliminary review.
required_dossiers: Articles of association notarized by a French notary
Proof of identity and address for shareholders and managers
Bank deposit certificate for minimum capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, provide additional documents or request an amendment to the articles within the prescribed period

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized articles, capital proof, manager details, and any other required forms to the online portal. Authorize the portal to process the filing. Monitor for registration confirmation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit any missing or corrected documents promptly or appeal the decision to the registry authority

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in Official Gazette and Issuance of SIREN/SIRET
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal Officiel and INPI Commercial and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once registered, publish the incorporation notice in the Journal Officiel de la République Française. Receive the SIREN and SIRET numbers. Update corporate documents and open bank accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request publication correction or re-publication if errors are identified

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Regional Directorate for Industry, Research and Environment (DRIRE)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Authorization for the Operation of a Dangerous Materials Testing Laboratory

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Regional Directorate for Environment, Planning and Housing (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with REACH regulations, UN38.3 testing protocols, VOC emission limits below 20 mg/m³, and proper hazardous waste management

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the SDIS, structural safety inspections, and occupational health clearance from the Prefecture

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); VAT registration is handled by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE). Portal: impots.gouv.fr / pro.impots.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities without an establishment in France must apply for VAT registration through the DGFiP’s SIE using Form CO (Cerfa n°14871*01) or via the EU’s One-Stop-Shop (OSS) for distance sales and certain B2B services. Non-EU entities must appoint an individual tax representative (assujetti unique) who is severally liable for VAT. The application requires an EORI number, proof of business activity, identity documents, and details of the fiscal representative. The SIE issues a French TIN and, where applicable, a TVA intracommunautaire number (FR followed by a two-digit control key and the SIREN number).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at entity level. It may elect, under strict statutory conditions (Art. 239 bis AA CGI), to be treated as a transparent pass-through entity for its first five fiscal years if its shareholders are individuals and annual turnover does not exceed specified thresholds. France does not apply a US-style check-the-box election. Hybrid mismatch elections must comply with EU ATAD 1 and ATAD 2 instruments transposed into the French General Tax Code, notably regarding reverse hybrid and branch mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for services for established French small businesses under the franchise en base; however, for non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in France, there is no statutory registration threshold and a VAT registration is mandatory (subject to reverse charge mechanisms for B2B services).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France imposes a progressive mandatory e-invoicing regime for B2B transactions from September 2026, requiring issuance and transmission through registered dematerialization platforms (PDPs) or the public Portal, with e-reporting of cross-border and B2C transaction data to the DGFiP via API. B2G invoices must be submitted to Chorus Pro. For retail cash operations, certified cash register software (logiciel de caisse) per Article 286 CGI must resist falsification; no real-time fiscal stamping is currently applied to general B2B VAT invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to exports of movable goods physically transferred or transported out of the European Union by the seller, the buyer, or a third party acting on their behalf, provided the goods leave EU territory and are not subject to installation or assembly tests altering their nature. For offensive and defensive testing laboratory services, zero-rating applies to services directly related to exported goods, while cross-border B2B testing services rendered to a VAT-registered non-French client are generally outside French VAT scope under reverse charge or taxed in the customer’s jurisdiction. The lab must retain documentary evidence of the contractual link, the destination, and the actual export of the tested goods within the required proof period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU / EAD) with MRN
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR transport document evidencing physical exit from the EU
Commercial Invoice and test report tied to the exact exported goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/FX settlement proof demonstrating payment in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or inadequately documented export zero-rating is subject to retrospective VAT reassessment (rappels), a 40% penalty for substantial inaccuracies or bad faith (or 80% in cases of concealed activity or abusive manoeuvres), and late-payment interest of 0.20% per month. Criminal exposure includes fines up to EUR 37,500 and imprisonment for tax fraud; the appointed tax representative is jointly and severally liable for VAT, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France / Direction Générale du Trésor
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible with both capital and current account operations liberalised under the EU Treaty and the French Monetary and Financial Code. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and liquidation proceeds are freely transferable to non-residents, subject only to domestic withholding tax obligations and statistical balance-of-payments reporting. There is no exchange control permission or surrender requirement for ordinary inbound or outbound trade and investment flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds and no statutory timeline for conversion into local currency. Export receipts may be held in foreign currency or euro indefinitely on the books of a French bank, must be collected through a regulated banking channel, and must be reported as part of the monthly or quarterly balance-of-payments declaration filed with the Banque de France under the 'Problematic' statistical regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Foreign Currency Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High viability for a low-risk professional testing laboratory, but subject to strict legal limitations. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) may support payment initiation and FX conversion services only if they are authorised in the European Economic Area and pass the French client review. They cannot operate as a deposit-taking credit institution, cannot provide the capital escrow guarantee expected by counterparties, and are not acceptable as the sole banking relation for the corporate entity. A French Tier-1 bank account or a bank account in a correspondent French clearing participant remains mandatory for statutory treasury operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the general manager and at least one other significative benficiary representative is required by most French Tier-1 banks; remote opening is accepted for low-risk professional clients using video-conference interview in a bank-certified e-KYC platform, but the second interview may need to be conducted in person at the registered office or a French notary bank's office. The company's registered office physical address, business substance, and satellite office lease are mandatory verification anchors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner without verifiable tax-residence data
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport or national ID, valid residence permit or tax residency certificate from the UBO's jurisdiction, French Kbis extract, and a certified beneficial ownership register filing with the French Companies Registry

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared testing business purpose and the treasury payment profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation certificate, UN38.3 testing scope contract, laboratory lease and equipment invoices, French Business register (Kbis) showing ISIC 7120, and an audited opening balance sheet

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border wire traffic from countries that are not the entity's declared client universe
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client list and testing service agreements, country-of-origin risk assessment, written payment flow description, and entity's internal AML controls policy with mandated sanctions screening

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal bank accounts for corporate receipts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory auditor certificate confirming no personal-account intermingling, corporate bank mandate drafts, FEC audit trail, and a detailed treasury policy approved by the managing partner

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are executed via standard SWIFT MT103 or SEPA credit transfer using the company's French IBAN. Recommended purpose codes include S301 for equity contribution, S010 for professional fees, and S018 for testing and analysis services. Verification must include targeted financial sanctions screening against French, EU, and UN lists, confirmation of the absence of a false positive on the beneficial owner, checks of the congruence between the payment reference and the signed testing service agreement, and collection of a certified copy of the VAT registration certificate for cross-border service receipts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlement uses SEPA Credit Transfer within the SEPA framework, SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA jurisdictions, and commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT707) for battery sample or calibration equipment procurement. The French bank must be granted a standing settlement instruction to convert invoices denominated in USD or CNY into euro, and all outbound wires must include the France's balance-of-payments reporting code to avoid regulatory rejection.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards for currencies freely traded in the European market, primarily USD, GBP, and CNY
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or low-liquidity emerging-market currencies when bilateral deliverability is not available
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for material multi-year testing contracts with significant deferred settlement risk
Plain vanilla European FX options for protecting a defined future cash-flow window without margin accounting complexity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements (Comptes Annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers formal notice; non-compliance after 3 months may result in court-ordered dissolution and fines up to 1,500 EUR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually if unchanged; within 1 month of any shareholding or control transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to 10,000 EUR; non-compliance may initiate administrative strike-off proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if turnover exceeds 50 million EUR, total assets exceed 43 million EUR, or employee count exceeds 50

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of UBO details to RCS if no changes; mandatory update within one month of any shareholding or control transfer

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced IS rate of 15% on the first €38,120 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover under €10m); Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to €100m and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% of eligible expenses up to €400k per annum; loss carryforward is indefinite, but limited in annual deduction to €1m plus 50% of the fraction of taxable profit exceeding €1m. Prior losses may be carried back 3 years (restricted to €1m).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD accompanied by annexes 2052-SD to 2059-SD and 2061-SD; electronic filing through the DGFiP's EDI/EFI teleprocedure or the online professional portal at impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years ending 31 December, the return is due by the second working day after 1 May of the following year. For any other fiscal year end, the return is due within three months of the closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form, SIREN/SIRET, NAF (APE) code, registered tax office, and VAT identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must insert the address and tax number of their French permanent establishment (PE), or their temporary tax number plus the name and address of the French tax representative if they are without a PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net book income or loss per the statutory accounts for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only include the profit or loss attributable to the French PE or the French-source service activities (UN38.3 battery test laboratory); do not consolidate foreign home-office results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal reinstatements (non-deductible expenses) and deductions (e.g. CIR, preferential depreciation) that convert book profit to taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign head-office costs are deductible only if incurred for the French PE and on an arm's-length basis; excessive intercompany royalty or interest payments must be re-added if not TP compliant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or carried-forward deficit before application of loss relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show profit subject to IS. A deficit generated by the French PE can be carried forward without time limit; a foreign tax loss cannot be used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year tax losses actually used in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule demonstrating the origin and availability of losses; a change in PE ownership may invalidate survival of the deficit if the business changes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Base imposable et impôt brut
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base plus computation of corporate income tax (IS), after applying the reduced SME rate and surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are taxed at the standard 25% rate, absent the SME reduced rate if the parent group's global revenue exceeds the ceiling; state any legal basis for rate mitigation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Crédits d'impôt et avoirs fiscaux
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research credit (CIR), innovation credit (CII), tax credits for competitions and cultural activities, and foreign-source tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident PE may claim CIR only for R&D physically carried out in France and subject to French corporate tax; foreign parent companies claiming CIR must be able to prove the French PE's command of the R&D operation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file: 10% penalty (40% if the return is not filed within 30 days after formal notice), plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month. Intentional concealment or fraudulent filing: 80% penalty. Failure to pay instalments: 5% penalty per unpaid instalment. Non-residents may also face loss of treaty benefits and fiscal representative disqualification.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% domestic withholding tax (Article 119 bis 2 CGI) on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders outside the EU/EEA or not covered by an applicable treaty; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if the parent holds more than 10% of capital for at least two years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the beneficial owner must (1) obtain a French 'certificat de résidence fiscale' via Form 5050 (or counterpart certificate in treaty partner), (2) submit tax residence certificate to the French paying agent before the payment, together with a statement of beneficial ownership, (3) where applicable, file Form 1057 for Parent-Subsidiary Directive exclusions, and (4) if the reduced rate is not applied at source, file a 'réclamation contentieuse' with the DGFiP for refund within two years of the end of the tax year, attaching proof of residence and date of dividend payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and patent/process payments to non-residents: statutory withholding at 33.33% (Article 125-0 CGI for certain non-domiciled patent royalties), commonly reduced under DTA to 0% or 5% depending on the treaty and cultural or industrial character of the IP. Interest on debt to non-residents: 0% statutory withholding in most cases; treaty-protected interest may be 0% if the lender is the beneficial owner and not capitalised or in a profit-sharing arrangement.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €400,000,000 (French Local File and Master File obligation threshold: annual group turnover or gross assets exceeding €400 million; CbCR threshold €750 million group consolidated revenue)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: ESR (Economic Substance Regulations) are a UAE-specific instrument and are not directly applicable in France. France applies substance-over-form through the general anti-abuse rule in Article L.64 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales (LPF), complemented by BEPS/civil law jurisprudence. For a French SARL engaged as a dangerous-goods testing laboratory, treaty benefits require actual personnel, premises, and decision-making in France. The absence of these factors gives the tax authorities power to recharacterize the SARL as a shell and attribute profits to a shareholder's country.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating taxable profit by failing to declare French-source UN38.3 testing fees, invoicing through a no-substance offshore vehicle, destroying lab records, or failing to file Form 2065 for more than three consecutive years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1741 CGI, fraud is punishable by up to five years' imprisonment (seven years when carried out through an intermediary established outside the EU) and a fine of €500,000 (or, if greater, 75% of the evaded tax). Tax penalties: 80% of the unpaid tax plus 0.20% per month late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director and de facto directors can be pursued under Article L.267 LPF for payment of the company's tax debts where they have been actively involved in fraudulent activities, with personal bank accounts frozen, travel bans, and imprisonment upon criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Profit Shifting and Transfer Pricing Abuses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive management fees, royalties, or testing toll fees to the French SARL for a shell parent that performs no laboratory work; failing to prepare Local/Master File when above the €400m threshold; unjustified dilution of profit margin to 0%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article L.13 AA LPF and Article 57 CGI, the DGFiP can re-determine arm's-length profit and impose a penalty of 100% of the redistributed profits if the enterprise cannot substantiate reasonableness (or 50% if failure to respond to a demand for TP documentation). Abuse-of-right penalty may reach 80% under Article 1729 CGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false TP documentation or act as intermediaries in a circular scheme can be held jointly liable for the tax assessed and exposed to a commercial court's 'action en comblement de passif' for managerial fault.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Substance / Abus de Droit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a French SARL with no physical facility, no qualified testing staff, and no real activity, while claiming CIR/CII credits for alleged R&D, and distributing all profit to an offshore shareholder without commercial rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGFiP may declare the arrangement an 'abus de droit' under Article L.64 LPF, disregard the scheme, and restore the true taxable base; the taxpayer faces an 80% anti-abuse penalty and a reopening of the statute of limitations to six years; CIR claims may be denied with interest and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly establishes a sham arrangement is personally liable for the reinstated taxes through abuse-of-right procedure; travel bans and director disqualification can be imposed in conjunction with criminal prosecution for organised fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash or wire transfers from unknown beneficial owners without KYC, performing UN38.3 certification tests for a customer subject to EU/UN sanctions, or issuing battery safety certificates without physical testing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Articles L.561-2 and L.562-1 CMF can result in administrative sanctions of up to €4 million or 10% of consolidated turnover for the entity; criminal money laundering (Article 324-1 Penal Code) carries up to ten years' imprisonment and €750,000 fine, with 50% additional confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly encourage or facilitate such activities face personal criminal liability, civil restitution for unjust enrichment, a travel ban pending prosecution, and a prohibition on managing commercial companies for five years or more.
